newsitem.title: UK: BAA climbs after results meet expectations.
newsitem.headline: BAA climbs after results meet expectations.

text.p: Shares in airports operator BAA Plc opened higher on Tuesday after first quarter earnings met with analysts expectations.
The shares were up 9-1/2p to 570p by 0731 GMT.
BAA said earlier that first-quarter, pre-tax profit was up 4.5 percent to 136 million stg, bang in line with consensus estimates.
But after tax, which included a one-off provision of 102 million stg for the windfall tax, profit was just three million compared with 98 million the previous year.

"The results were pretty much as expected," said Nigel Davies, transport analyst at Panmure Gordon. "But if you adjust the figures for the rebalance of the landing charges, then operating profit would have been up 10.8 percent and traffic growth of 7.8 percent was significant."
Analysts said the windfall tax liability was in line with forecasts and they welcomed the speedy one-off allowance for this charge.

"The shares look cheap at these levels," Davies said. "They are only on a six percent premium to the market where historically they have traded up to a 35 percent premium and we certainly prefer them to British Airways."
The analyst said today's earnings would not prompt any revision in his forecasts though he remains a buyer of the stock.

"BAA are also a closet property company with an external net asset value of 621p a share," said Davies. "Other property majors are trading at a ten percent premium to their asset value so I think a fair value for BAA would be around 620p."
